data.why: ConText ships no corpus of its own and needs a built 'conc' corpus and reference corpus to show anything; these six short parliamentary-style speeches on autonomous weapons policy (the study corpus) and six short unrelated news items (the reference corpus) are built into conc's on-disk corpus format by seed/build_corpus.py during install, since conc requires pre-built corpora rather than loading raw text at request time.

goals: identify which words or phrases are distinctively frequent in the target corpus compared with a reference corpus (keyness analysis)
read concordance lines for a keyword in context, sorted and reordered by surrounding words
find the collocates of a search term to understand its typical company
find the recurring multi-word clusters/n-grams a term appears in
drill from a concordance line or cluster back into the full original text to see it in context
compare two corpora quickly by switching which corpus and reference corpus are loaded

review.summary: The tree maps ConText's keyness → in-context → source-text → compare workflow well, with sensible phases and faithful labels, and most cited screens show what their nodes claim. Before filing, fix two wrong citations (032 on the 'autonomous' tasks, 030 on the forward keyword task) and add nodes for the README's hyperlink drill-down and cluster narrowing, which the build blocked but which are central to the tool.
